newsitem.title: INDIA: India police crackdown nets 550 before Miss World.
newsitem.headline: India police crackdown nets 550 before Miss World.

text.p: Indian police said on Saturday they had detained about 550 people to head off potential trouble at the Miss World beauty pageant but a squad of would-be suicide protesters was still at large.
"It is a most bizarre situation," Julia Morley, the Miss World organiser, said.

Police in this southern Indian city rounded up militant Hindu nationalists, communists and various other protesters, but were still hunting a group of 15 women who have threatened to burn themselves alive to protest against the show.
Shortly before midnight (1830 GMT) one of the 88 young women contestants will win the Miss World title, marking the end of two fraught weeks beset by protests.

Bangalore police commissioner S.C. Burman said the city, patrolled by more than 10,000 police and paramilitary personnel, was quiet and there was little response to a strike call. On Friday a court ruled the armed forces could be used if needed to keep the peace.
But Miss World organisers remain alarmed by the threat of self-immolation by members of Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for Awakening Women) led by Kinay Narayana Shashikala.
Shashikala has gone into hiding since Thursday, but members of the right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) say they are in contact with her.
"We are looking for her. We will take her into custody when we track her down," Burman said.
One man has already turned himself into a human torch to protest against the pageant being staged in India. But that was last week in Tamil Nadu, hundreds of miles away from Bangalore.
The protesters say the beauty contest demeans women and threatens Indian culture.
Around two billion television viewers are expected to watch the three-hour show, which will include hundreds of extras plus elephants and a massive Hindu temple stage set.

The police are also on guard for a hitherto unknown group calling itself the Indian Tigers, which has claimed responsibility for attacks on the Indian organisers of Miss World and two small bomb blasts in which no one was injured.

Among those detained on Saturday were members of a "front organisation" for the Peoples War Group (PWG), a Naxalite Maoist rebel movement which has killed several policemen in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh state, Burman said.
Shashikala has said her followers will mingle with the 20,000 crowd in Chinnaswamy cricket stadium, the open-air venue for the event, and set fire to themselves after first taking poison.
Large numbers of police armed with guns and teargas swarmed around the cricket stadium, and 150 mobile patrols scoured the city for signs of trouble.
Pramila Nesargi, a state legislator, said she plans a "Miss Poverty, Miss Illiteracy" pageant outside the stadium this evening.

As if the potential for trouble were not great enough, even the weather is conspiring against the organisers, who on Saturday were busy buying umbrellas as a precaution against the overcast skies shrouding the open-air stadium.
